title: Maximum Score of a Node Sequence
summary: Given an undirected graph with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, and a scores array, find the maximum score of a valid node sequence of length 4.
statement: Given an undirected graph with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, and a scores array, find the maximum score of a valid node sequence of length 4. A valid sequence must have edges between every pair of adjacent nodes and no node repeated. If no such sequence exists, return -1.
constraints: Choose four distinct nodes a,b,c,d with edges a-b, b-c, and c-d.
The sequence score is the sum of all four node scores.
Return the maximum score, or -1 when no valid four-node sequence exists.
hints: Treat every edge b-c as the middle of a possible four-node sequence.
Only the three highest-score neighbors of each middle endpoint are needed because at most two nodes are forbidden by distinctness.
For each edge, try pairs from its endpoints’ top-three neighbor lists and keep sums whose four nodes are distinct.
Any optimal outer choice below third place would have three better neighbors, and at most two conflict, so some equally feasible better choice must exist.
editorial: Any optimal outer choice below third place would have three better neighbors, and at most two conflict, so some equally feasible better choice must exist.

tests.explanation: No chain can contain four distinct nodes, so return negative one.
